Kai (Sales): Hey team — Prospect NovaHealth wants a short POC next week. They need: mixed workload (chat + embeddings), multi-region failover, and KMS-backed keys. Can we confirm a load plan + expected cost delta for quantized vs fp16 models?
Alex S. (SE): Quick notes: target sustained 150 qps, bursts to 600 qps for ~2m windows. Chat requests ~120 tokens avg, embeddings 1k vector requests at 5k tokens total per minute.
Maya (PM): They want a writeup for execs: tail latency p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and risk matrix for KMS impact. Also security questionnaire asking for KMS key rotation policy.
Jules (SRE): We should test in us-west1 + eu-west1 and validate cross-region fallback <250ms added latency. Also test cold-starts for dedicated pools.
Alex S. (SE): Proposed load plan (short):
```
- Stage A (smoke): 10m, 10 qps (chat only)
- Stage B (ramp): 30m, ramp 10 -> 150 qps steady (chat heavy)
- Stage C (burst): 3 windows of 2m at 600 qps (mixed)
- Stage D (embeddings soak): 20m, 200 embeddings qps (vector route)
- Stage E (failover): terminate west pool, route to eu, measure added latency
```
Kai (Sales): Can you add the commands for our load generator (kgen) so ops can run it? Also include how to toggle quantized model.
Alex S. (SE): kgen example: `kgen --profile chat --qps 150 --duration 1800 --model redwood-chat-v1-fp16 --region us-west1`
To run quantized: `--model redwood-chat-v1-q8`
And embeddings: `kgen --profile embed --qps 200 --model redwood-embed-v1-q4 --region eu-west1`
Jules (SRE): I'll handle multi-region failover steps: 1) drain us-west1 route 2) bump weight to eu-west1 3) monitor p95/p99 and KV cache warmup. Expect ~120-250ms added for first 10k requests due to cache miss.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy of redwood-chat-v1-q8 to dedicated-us-west1 started — 12 GPU workers coming up :rocket:
Maya (PM): Pricing note for execs: rough delta (est): fp16 baseline $0.045 per 1k tokens, q8 approx 0.032 per 1k tokens (30% savings) but expect ~5-12% higher tail latency under burst without extra pooling. Include cost of KMS calls: negligible token cost but added 5-15ms per request for external KMS.
Alex S. (SE): Early results from a quick internal run (summary):
- steady 150 qps chat (fp16): p95 62ms, p99 132ms, tokens/sec ~27k
- steady 150 qps chat (q8): p95 74ms, p99 165ms, tokens/sec ~25k
- burst 600 qps mixed (q8, default pool): p95 210ms, p99 1.1s, observed queueing.
- embeddings soak (eu): 200 qps embeddings v1-q4: p95 48ms, p99 120ms
- failover (us -> eu): immediate added median 180ms, p99 spike to 1.4s during cache warmup
Alex S. (SE): Action items:
- Jules to run full POC in staging with the load plan and save traces to S3 (slo-team/poc/nova/5812)
- Maya to draft exec summary with cost table and risk matrix
- Kai to confirm schedule with prospect (preferred Wed 09:00 PT)
- SE to include KMS latency tests and rotated-key run
Jules (SRE): Will run 2x 3hr windows (one fp16 baseline, one q8) across both regions and attach perf dashboard + flamegraphs. Expect results by EOD Tuesday.
Kai (Sales): Also FYI prospect asked whether we support HSM-backed keys and whether that affects latency. Answer: yes, but add 10-30ms per request depending on HSM provider — include in risk matrix.
Maya (PM): One more ask from legal: sample SOC2 control mapping for POC data retention. Alex, can you paste the short blurb?
Alex S. (SE): "For POC runs we store logs and traces for 30 days in a customer-segregated bucket, access logged and restricted to ops team. We can extend to 90 days on request."
Kai (Sales): Perfect. I'll loop in prospect and propose Wed 09:00 PT. If anyone sees blockers call them out now. :thumbsup:
Jules (SRE): No blockers from infra. Will need a short quota bump for dedicated pool during burst windows — filing ticket now.
Alex S. (SE): I'll prepare the results writeup template (p95/p99 table, cost per 1M tokens, notes on KMS/HSM impacts, recommendation). Link when ready: https://redwood.internal/poc/writeups/5812
Maya (PM): Thanks everyone — keep updates in this thread so we can snap the exec summary after the runs.
Kai (Sales): Thanks — assigning follow-ups and will update prospect after Jules posts dashboards.
